newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis sees no quarrel with Bonn on EMU council.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis sees no quarrel with Bonn on EMU council.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Monday he did not have the impression there were differences between Paris and Bonn over France's call for a stability council to co-ordinate economic policies under European monetary union.
"I have discussed this with our European partners and the idea of setting up an informal stability and growth council has the support of some of our partners," he told a news conference.
Pressed on whether the German government supported the French proposal, Arthuis said, "I did not get the feeling there were differences on this."

France's call for a stability council to co-ordinate economic policies among countries inside European economic and monetary union has come under fire from the Bundesbank which fears it might undermine the independence of the future European Central Bank.
But officials from France and elsewhere have said the proposal has the support of the German government.
Arthuis, in an apparent reference to the Bundesbank comments, said that comments from an independent central bank did not commit the government to the same position.
"The Bank is independent. When a governor, whoever he is, makes a statement, I do not see that this commits the government," he said. "The Bank is independent, but so is the government," he added.

French officials said earlier that the stability council would fully respect the independence of the central bank and the principle of "subsidiarity", in which power is devolved whenever possible to the national level.
